articles.title: Home Assistant puts household players in Android’s media controls
articles.dek: Choose speakers and players to control from the notification shade, without opening a dashboard.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app exposes selected household media players in Android’s native media controls. Track information, artwork and playback position appear in the notification shade, with playback, track-skipping and seeking controls when the player supports them.

The Companion app’s Media controls setting lets the owner choose one or several players, with a separate notification for each. Fletcher D introduces the controls in his first contribution to Home Assistant’s Android app; Timothy corrects artwork loading.

pullRequests.title: Add native Android media controls for HA media_player entities
Fix typo in JPEG quality for loading art work in HaMediaSession

media.alt: Home Assistant media controls in the Android notification shade

articles.title: Music Assistant stops large album covers exhausting the server
articles.dek: A playback test with skips reduced peak memory from 5.2 GB to 459 MB.
body: Music Assistant prevents large album covers from exhausting a small server’s memory while music plays. Beta users on 4 GB Home Assistant hosts reported the add-on stopping after a few skips through music they had not played before.

Marcel van der Veldt makes the colours behind the now-playing screen come from a small cached thumbnail instead of the full-size cover. In a playback test with supplied music files and repeated skips, peak server memory fell from 5.2 GB to 459 MB. A related correction passes original-size JPEG covers through without unnecessarily decoding and recreating them.

pullRequests.title: Fix the server running out of memory on large album covers
Serve original-size JPEG artwork without re-encoding it

articles.title: Home Assistant offers a safer path to newer connection encryption
articles.dek: Existing HTTPS setups keep their compatibility until the owner chooses an upgrade, with automatic recovery if it locks them out.
body: Home Assistant gives owners who serve its interface over HTTPS a choice of updated encryption profiles without silently breaking older clients. Existing installations retain their previous profile; a repair offers a newer one, and a five-minute trial restores the old setting if the change locks the owner out.

The recommended Modern v6 profile requires TLS 1.3, while Intermediate v6 also accepts TLS 1.2 for older devices. New installations default to Modern v6. The network settings explain the choices and identify the older profiles as outdated.
The change concerns Home Assistant’s own web server. Returning to an older Home Assistant release requires restoring a backup because the saved settings use new profile names.

pullRequests.title: Version http SSL profiles and offer upgrade to Mozilla v6 via repair
Offer versioned SSL profiles in the HTTP server settings
Document the versioned HTTP SSL profiles

articles.title: Home Assistant gives AI clients a read-only connection
articles.dek: A new option removes tools that can change things from the configured MCP endpoint.
body: Home Assistant’s Model Context Protocol server gains a read-only option for giving AI clients access without allowing changes. When enabled, the configured endpoint lists only tools marked read-only and refuses calls to the others.
The option starts off and applies to the configured Model Context Protocol endpoint. Endpoints dedicated to an individual API keep their existing permissions.

pullRequests.title: Add read-only option to the MCP server
Document the MCP server read-only option

articles.title: ESPHome prevents overlapping updates from breaking its firmware
articles.dek: A second upload is refused while the first is writing, including the wait before restart.
body: ESPHome refuses a second wireless firmware upload while another is running. A command-line update and a web upload could previously write over each other; on ESP8266, that could leave a damaged image that needed a cable to reinstall.

Frédéric Metrich adds a shared lock across the update paths. It lasts until the successful update restarts the device, while an interrupted web upload releases it. The correction also prevents overlapping uploads from cancelling or disrupting updates on ESP32, LibreTiny and RP2040. The protection covers ESPHome’s own firmware updates; components that install firmware on a separate attached chip still need to adopt it.

pullRequests.title: [ota] Refuse a second OTA while one is already running

articles.title: ESPHome opens device controls on a phone without internet
articles.dek: An access-point-only device carries its own interface instead of showing a blank page.
body: ESPHome lets a device configured only as a Wi-Fi access point open its controls directly on a connected phone, without internet. Its web interface is embedded in the firmware instead of being loaded from an unreachable website.

Joining the device’s network opens the control page automatically when it uses the standard web port. J. Nick Koston verified live readings, switches and logs on ESP32 and ESP8266 with an iPhone. Devices that normally join a home network and only use an access point as a fallback retain their existing behavior unless the local interface is explicitly enabled.

pullRequests.title: [web_server] Self contained AP mode: embedded interface served as a captive portal
[web_server] Document access point mode

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps ESPHome speakers connected through their upgrade
articles.dek: Encrypted identities inherit the existing player, keeping groups and Home Assistant automations intact.
body: Music Assistant preserves an ESPHome Sendspin speaker’s existing player when an update changes its identity for encrypted connections. Its settings move to the new identity while the player identifier stays the same, keeping groups and Home Assistant automations attached to the speaker.

Maxim Raznatovski tests an Apollo CAST-1 moving from ESPHome 2026.9.1 to 2026.10.0b3. The migration operates with the default legacy-client compatibility setting enabled and also preserves Home Assistant names and announcements. Earlier beta attempts can leave an empty duplicate player to delete; previously disabled speakers still appear as a new player.

pullRequests.title: Fix updated ESPHome Sendspin speakers reappearing as new players

articles.title: Home Assistant makes custom entity names follow their devices
articles.dek: Dashboard names may grow longer; old spoken names are preserved as aliases.
body: Home Assistant extends dynamic device naming to entities that an owner has named. Renaming the device then updates those entities too, while dashboard cards, badges and rows without an explicit name use the device name followed by the entity name.

An entity called Ceiling light on a device called Hue bulb therefore appears as Hue bulb Ceiling light. To keep a short label, rename the device and choose Use device name for the entity, or set a name on the card. Area views also stop stripping the area name automatically.

The migration removes a device prefix already present in an entity name to avoid doubling it. Previous names remain aliases for Assist, Alexa and Google Assistant, preserving familiar spoken requests through the change.

pullRequests.title: Migrate user-given entity names
Preserve pre-migration entity names as aliases in voice assistants
Finalize the entity naming migration
Remove name prefix stripping from generated dashboards

articles.title: ESPHome lets ESP32 devices sleep between ordinary work
articles.dek: Optional automatic light sleep and CPU scaling give makers control over idle power.
body: ESPHome adds power management for ESP32 devices using ESP-IDF, allowing the processor to slow down and optionally enter light sleep when its main loop is idle. Supported chips can also power down peripherals and flash during sleep.

In a measured ESP32-C6 Fire Beetle setup acting as a sleepy OpenThread end device, polling every 180 seconds and waking its main loop every 30 seconds, average current was about 105 microamps over an hour. That result describes the tested configuration, rather than every ESPHome device.

Automatic light sleep starts disabled and must be selected by the maker. The configuration checks which power-down options the chip supports; powering down flash is unavailable when external PSRAM is configured.

[power_management] Document the power_management domain and the esp32_power_management platform

articles.title: Home Assistant stops MQTT events running automations twice
articles.dek: Reloading the connection or enabling a disabled entity no longer leaves duplicate subscriptions behind.
body: Home Assistant corrects a failure that made a discovered MQTT device trigger run its automation twice for one message after a connection reload. Discovered tag scanners could likewise report a single scan twice, even though the broker delivered the message only once.

The correction removes the old trigger and scanner subscriptions before restoring the connection. It also covers the automatic reload shortly after enabling a disabled MQTT entity; previously, restarting Home Assistant cleared the duplicates.

pullRequests.title: Fix MQTT device triggers and tags firing twice after reload

articles.title: Music Assistant makes AI Radio shows playable from Home Assistant
articles.dek: Shows join the Radio library as finite programmes, with favourites and shortcuts.
body: Music Assistant represents AI Radio shows as ordinary radio items, letting them appear in the Radio library, receive favourites and shortcuts, and start through Home Assistant’s normal playback action. A show’s fixed track list plays to its end instead of continuing through Autoplay.

Marvin Schenkel coordinates the server and interface: a show’s page lists its tracks, the card shows when it is on air, and stopping it clears the selected queue. The host joins for that show and leaves when it finishes or is replaced. The opening spoken introduction is not included in this playback path.

articles.title: Home Assistant stops Android tracking when it is switched off
articles.dek: Disabling location or activity tracking properly unregisters the background work.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app properly stops its background location and activity tracking when the owner disables those features. Previously, it did not reliably unregister the tracking work after either setting was switched off.
The correction handles both tracking paths. Previously, activity tracking was expected to stop after restarting the app.

articles.title: Sendspin keeps grouped speakers aligned after audio stalls
articles.dek: Corrections also smooth the handover when speakers join a playing group.
body: Sendspin’s Python server corrects timing failures that could leave grouped speakers audibly out of step after audio production stalled. Different formats could end up 15 to 357 milliseconds apart, and pausing and restarting did not always realign them.

Maxim Raznatovski makes the audio paths follow the same timing changes and closes gaps when a speaker catches up to an ongoing stream. Music Assistant also corrects a separate handover that could leave a speaker using equalizer filters about 100 milliseconds behind when it joined a group.

articles.title: Home Assistant ends Tailscale’s recurring token replacement
articles.dek: Existing connections need a one-time switch to OAuth client credentials.
body: Home Assistant’s Tailscale connection switches to OAuth client credentials, removing the recurring need to replace API access tokens that expire after at most ninety days. Connections using an old token stop loading and request the replacement credentials when this change reaches their installation.

The migration preserves the integration entry and removes its old token. The OAuth client needs only Devices: Core — Read permission; its short-lived access tokens are renewed automatically. This is ra8844’s first contribution to home-assistant/core.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps local music reads inside their chosen folder
articles.dek: Scanning and playback use the same opened file that passed the access check.
body: Music Assistant strengthens the boundary around a Local files source so playback, artwork and library scanning read only files inside its chosen folder. It checks the file it actually opens and hands that same open file to its media tools, avoiding a second lookup of a path that could have changed.

Marcel van der Veldt applies the check when playback starts, including queued tracks and every seek, and to multi-file audiobooks, lyrics, playlists and folder scans. WebDAV and cloud sources keep their existing URL-based playback.

articles.title: Home Assistant removes scheduled locations from Tesla diagnostics
articles.dek: Charging and preconditioning schedules stop exposing coordinates in troubleshooting exports.
body: Home Assistant redacts location coordinates embedded in Tesla charging and preconditioning schedules from Teslemetry and Tesla Fleet diagnostic files. Those schedules can identify places such as home or work even when the vehicle’s current driving coordinates have already been hidden.
The correction covers coordinates within schedule lists and the flattened schedule fields. It changes the exported troubleshooting data, rather than removing the schedules from the vehicle.

articles.title: ESPHome sends local commands to Somfy blinds and awnings
articles.dek: A compatible radio transmitter can act as a paired remote, with a saved rolling code.
body: ESPHome adds commands for Somfy RTS blinds, shutters and awnings through a 433.42 MHz transmitter. An automation can send up, down, My and pairing commands instead of relying on a separate remote.

The accompanying guide explains pairing ESPHome as a new remote and retaining the rolling code across restarts. This is a transmit-only connection: it does not receive the blind’s position or decode its remote. This is RobertH1993’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Music Assistant plays an artist’s albums in release order
articles.dek: Listeners can choose albums instead of an automatic shuffle of tracks.
body: Music Assistant adds an order setting for starting an artist: shuffled tracks, albums in random order, or albums from oldest to newest. Album playback follows the existing album-playback settings, providing a way to listen through a career rather than jump between songs.

Zsolt limits that sequence to albums credited to the artist, excluding singles and provider-only compilations. An album present in several sources plays once. Shuffled tracks remain the default, and an explicit shuffle request still takes priority.

articles.title: Sendspin’s Python player allows unpaired servers by default
articles.dek: Existing installations must turn off unpaired access if they want to keep requiring it.
body: Sendspin’s Python command-line player starts accepting unpaired music servers by default, including installations that already have a pairing file. The change avoids requiring someone to find a pairing code in a headless player’s log after an upgrade.
To keep requiring pairing, owners need to set --unpaired-access false. Maxim Raznatovski adds the corresponding saved setting.

articles.title: ESPHome changes encrypted update keys without a cable
articles.dek: The uploader can authenticate with the old key while installing firmware that uses its replacement.
body: ESPHome adds a direct way to rotate the key used for encrypted wireless firmware updates. Put the replacement in the normal key setting and the previous value in the old-key setting; the uploader can reconnect with the previous key while installing firmware built with the new one.

The device stores only the new key. After a successful installation, the command-line tool reports that the old key can be removed. A separate option can prompt privately for a different key for one upload, without putting it in a command-line argument.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows when Dexcom actually took a reading
articles.dek: A separate timestamp distinguishes measurement age from the last change in its value.
body: Home Assistant adds the time Dexcom recorded a glucose reading, allowing a dashboard to show the measurement’s age. An unchanged value previously left ordinary state-change timestamps behind, while a fresh cloud poll could still be retrieving an older measurement.

The new Glucose reading time sensor uses the timestamp supplied by Dexcom rather than the time Home Assistant polled or last saw a different value. This is Victor Kuznetsov’s first contribution to home-assistant/core.

articles.title: ESPHome turns compatible ESP32 boards into USB keyboards
articles.dek: Button actions can send ordinary keys and media commands to a connected computer.
body: ESPHome adds a USB keyboard component for ESP32 boards with USB OTG hardware. Makers can connect physical buttons or other automations to ordinary key presses, modifiers and media commands such as volume up.

The component holds one ordinary key at a time and supplies separate press and release actions. It cannot yet share the USB connection with ESPHome’s USB serial component; combining those functions requires further work. This is Frederik Bolding’s first contribution to ESPHome.
